papers.title: PtychoFM: A Foundation Model for Ptychographic Imaging
authors: Aileen Luo, Emon Dey, Ming Du, Tao Zhou, Peco Myint, Himanshu Goel, Shashank Subramanian, Xiangyu Yin, Tekin Bicer, Sini\v{s}a Veseli, Cheng-Chu Chung, Jeffrey A. Klug, Aldo Pe\~na P\'erez, Lloren\c{c} Fanals-i-Batllori, Christopher Kenney, Henry Shi, Lorenzo Rota, Angelo Dragone, Zirui Gao, Douglas A. Bennett, John A. B. Mates, Leila R. Vale, Michael R. Vissers, Yi Jiang, Junjing Deng, Tejas Guruswamy, Varuni K. Sastry, Bowen Zheng, Takenori Shimamura, Oliver Hoidn, Aashwin Mishra, Hannah Parraga, Brandon Stone, Jonathan Baldwin, Aaron Michelson, Michael Wojcik, Xiaoyin Zheng, Robert Underwood, Yijiang Li, Jinxing Jiang, Nicholas Schwarz, Apurva Mehta, Johanna Nelson Weker, Hassina Bilheux, Joel N. Ullom, Alexander Hexemer, Antonino Miceli, Kibaek Kim, Hanfei Yan, Mathew J. Cherukara, Alec R. Sandy, Stefan Vogt, Laurent C. Chapon
papers.abstract: Ptychography provides high-resolution lensless imaging across X-ray, electron, and optical microscopy, but reconstructing images from diffraction measurements generally requires computationally intensity iterative phase retrieval. These methods often require experiment-specific analysis, limiting real-time feedback as data acquisition rates increase. Here, we demonstrate PtychoFM, a physics-aware foundation model for ptychographic imaging that combines large-scale pre-training with experiment-specific fine-tuning to reconstruct complex object images directly from individual diffraction patterns. Trained using a differentiable forward model without object-space labels, PtychoFM transfers from step-scan training data on one sample to fly-scan measurements of other samples with different feature sizes, morphologies, and refraction indices. At a synchrotron beamline, diffraction frames were streamed from the detector to a single GPU for inference at up to 200 frames per second and returned for real-time visualization. PtychoFM provides a practical route to rapid, transferable ptychographic reconstruction and live experimental feedback under nonideal conditions.
papers.tldr: PtychoFM is a physics-aware foundation model that combines large-scale pre-training with experiment-specific fine-tuning to reconstruct ptychographic images directly from individual diffraction patterns without object-space labels, enabling transferable, real-time reconstruction at up to 200 frames per second.

papers.title: Toward light-controlled transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams
authors: Yiming Pan, Jiapeng Yang, Hao Geng
papers.abstract: Kinetic fluctuations and space-charge expansion hinder Wigner ordering in free-electron beams. Here we propose a laser-driven route toward transient, substrate-free Wigner ordering that combines photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) attosecond bunching, synchronized magnetic focusing, and spatial preconditioning. Classical relaxation and zero-temperature fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo trap benchmarks show that sixfold order survives quantum fluctuations from 1 T to sub-Tesla fields, defining ultrafast preparation targets.
papers.tldr: The paper proposes a laser-driven, substrate-free route to transient transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams by combining PINEM bunching, synchronized magnetic focusing, and spatial preconditioning, with benchmarks showing that sixfold order survives quantum fluctuations from 1 T down to sub-Tesla fields.

papers.title: Mixing and Preserving Properties of Non-van der Waals 2D Materials in Sandwich-like Heterostructures
authors: Anastasiia Nihei, Rico Friedrich
papers.abstract: Heterostructure interfaces created by stacking two-dimensional (2D) materials outline an appealing route towards achieving advanced electronic and magnetic functionalities at the nanoscale. Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) sandwich-like heterostructures (HSs) are build out of non-vdW 2D materials derived from non-layered crystals and establish a new frontier enabling strong interfacial coupling. Employing ab initio density functional theory (DFT), we investigate two classes of such trilayer HSs: purely non-vdW assemblies and hybrid vdW/non-vdW/vdW stacks. We show that non-vdW sandwiches undergo pronounced geometric reconstruction forming chemically bonded interfaces with large absolute binding energies up to an order of magnitude larger than those of conventional vdW HSs. These strong interactions drive extensive electronic hybridization, band gap renormalization, and tunable interlayer magnetic coupling. In contrast, vdW encapsulation largely protects the intrinsic atomic and electronic structure of the non-vdW sheet from the environment , while enabling charge transfer doping of the vdW layers. Our results thus establish sandwich HSs a versatile interface design platform, spanning interaction regimes from weakly perturbed encapsulation to strongly interacting chemically bonded systems with emergent electronic and magnetic behavior.
papers.tldr: Using DFT, the paper shows that purely non-vdW 2D sandwich heterostructures form strongly chemically bonded interfaces with enhanced hybridization, band-gap renormalization, and tunable magnetic coupling, whereas vdW encapsulation largely preserves the non-vdW layer while enabling charge-transfer doping, establishing sandwich heterostructures as a versatile platform spanning weak encapsulation to strong interfacial coupling.

papers.title: Topological terahertz fields from tunable vectorial currents
authors: Jacob Pettine, Tae Gwan Park, Yanhe Lyu, Wangke Yu, John B. Maier, Matthew Yeung, Rujuta Sane, Chun-Chieh Chang, Nuh Gedik, Yijie Shen, Hou-Tong Chen
papers.abstract: Future information processing calls for photonic architectures with greater capacity, intrinsic resilience to noise, and direct integration with quantum materials and devices. Topological light pulses have recently emerged as promising candidates to meet these demands, yet the complexity underlying their unique properties also makes them challenging to generate, tune, and fully resolve in space and time. Here, we generate and actively tune topological light fields through transient vectorial currents in an optoelectronic metasurface. Incident linear polarization steers the local direction of photocurrents in graphene via nanoplasmonic resonators with triangular symmetry, while a global winding pattern enables continuous tuning between compressional and circulating charge flows. Under ultrafast excitation, these currents radiate single-cycle terahertz toroidal pulses spanning electric- and magnetic-dominant modes with dynamically evolving skyrmion textures. Full spatiotemporal mapping and reconstruction provide a complete visualization of the toroidal structure of light, directly tracing the closed field surfaces while continuously tracking skyrmion number and helicity throughout a single cycle. These results connect two-dimensional vectorial currents to rich three-dimensional electromagnetic field structures, while establishing a versatile integrated platform for higher-dimensional photonic information processing and emerging material spectroscopies.
papers.tldr: Using polarization-controlled vectorial photocurrents in a graphene-based plasmonic metasurface, the authors generate and continuously tune single-cycle terahertz toroidal light pulses whose electric- and magnetic-field skyrmion textures are fully resolved in space and time.
affiliations: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Moir\'e-Induced Interlayer Electron-Phonon Coupling in Graphene/hBN Superlattices
authors: Dasol Kim, Zhengguang Lu, Tonghang Han, Guorui Chen, Tianyi Han, Jixiang Yang, Bing Cheng, Zhenxian Liu, Christopher Homes, G. L. Carr, Jeong Min Park, Qihang Zhang, Lili Jiang, Hongyuan Li, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Feng Wang, Long Ju
papers.abstract: Electron-phonon coupling (EPC) plays a vital role in the electrical and optical properties of materials, ranging from superconductivity to charge dynamics. In moir\'e superlattices, out-of-plane vibrations can modulate the moir\'e potential and enhance interlayer EPC. Here we report the first direct observation of a resonance arising from coupling between moir\'e electronic excitations and phonons in graphene-based moir\'e superlattices. Using Fourier-transform infrared photocurrent spectroscopy, we detect the nominally silent hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) out-of-plane optical (ZO) phonon as a pronounced absorption peak. The phonon interferes with moir\'e flat-band excitations to form a characteristic Fano resonance. Displacement field-dependent measurements confirm that the feature originates from coupling to the moir\'e electronic continuum rather than simple zone folding. We further observe similar resonances in devices with different graphene layer numbers and twist configurations. This enhanced EPC provides a pathway for understanding and controlling emerging quantum phenomena, such as superconductivity, and engineering novel optoelectronic devices.
papers.tldr: The paper reports the first direct observation of a Fano resonance from interlayer electron-phonon coupling between moiré flat-band excitations in graphene and the normally silent out-of-plane phonon of hBN in graphene/hBN superlattices, revealing an enhanced coupling pathway for controlling quantum and optoelectronic phenomena.

papers.title: Compositionally Tunable Synthesis of High-Entropy Transition Metal Dichalcogenides Exhibiting Above-Room-Temperature Magnetism
authors: Chen Zhang, Xiahua Zhong, Dejia Kong, Wenhu Wang, Christopher T. Nelson, Mingfeng Chen, Xiaoqing He, Benjamin J. Lawrie, Hsin-Yun Chao, Alex L. Melendez, Peixin Liu, Benjamin G. Gibson, Xiaodong Yan, Xi Wang, Liangbo Liang, Zheng Gai, Huan Zhao, Yingchao Yang
papers.abstract: As silicon-based electronics approach their physical limits, low-dimensional magnetic materials have attracted increasing attention for next-generation electronic and information technologies. Realizing these opportunities requires two-dimensional (2D) materials with robust and tunable room-temperature magnetism. Here, we report a two-step synthesis strategy for fabricating 2D high-entropy transition metal dichalcogenides (HE-TMDs) incorporating magnetic elements beyond conventional groups 4-6. High-entropy layered double hydroxides (HE-LDHs) are first synthesized via hydrothermal coprecipitation, enabling atomic-level mixing of diverse transition metals across groups 4-12. Subsequent chalcogenization yields 2D HE-TMDs while preserving homogeneous elemental distribution. This approach circumvents the constraints of solid-state reaction, chemical vapor transport methods, enabling the synthesis of compositionally complex and structurally controlled 2D magnets. Representative (VCrFeCoNi)S2-x exhibits robust magnetism above room temperature, demonstrating the potential of this high-entropy design strategy for expanding the compositional and functional diversity of 2D magnetic materials.
papers.tldr: A two-step high-entropy LDH-to-TMD synthesis enables compositionally tunable 2D transition metal dichalcogenides with robust above-room-temperature magnetism.

papers.title: A recursive self-improvement framework for electron microscopy analysis
authors: Yaotian Yang, Sijia Tao, Yuping Zhang, Jiangjie Qiu, Qinghua Zhang, Xiao Chen, Fei Wei
papers.abstract: Resolving local atomic structures such as defects and interfaces from electron microscopy contrast relies heavily on researcher judgement, leading to low efficiency and subjective standards. Here we present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided and expert-informed recursive self-improvement framework that turns one-off human corrections into reusable, verifiable capabilities by updating executable operators, parameters and routing rules with versioned inheritance. Given researcher-defined tasks, the system selects analysis paths from image features without expert labels, while testing and inheriting code updates under fixed budgets. Combining physical priors with expert feedback improves atomic point-defect detection over larger models and raises cross-material interface coverage from 5.13% to 72.11% within a 10% area budget. Adapting the framework to micrographs from unseen studies further separates touching nanoparticles by aligning optimization with particle-level measurements. This work moves computational microscopy beyond standalone models and static scripts towards self-evolving platforms that accumulate human scientific expertise
papers.tldr: The paper introduces PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided, expert-informed recursive self-improvement framework for electron microscopy that converts one-off human corrections into reusable, verifiable analysis capabilities through versioned inheritance of operators, parameters, and routing rules, enabling self-evolving microscopy platforms with improved defect detection and interface coverage.

papers.title: A library-based approach for inverse reconstruction of cavity depth using angle-resolved cathodoluminescence
authors: Sam T. P. Borman, Daphne M. Dekker, Evelijn Akerboom, Albert Polman
papers.abstract: In nanofabrication processes, accurate metrology is a crucial step for obtaining control over the required critical dimensions in a device. Traditionally, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is used to obtain high resolution measurements of the lateral dimension, but obtaining depth information on a thick sample is more complex. In this work, we use angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (AR-CL) spectroscopy to resolve this third dimension. Using 30 keV electrons in the SEM, CL is created at the bottom of a micrometer scale cavity milled in a gold surface. We show that reflections of the CL off the cavity sidewalls produce an interferogram which is a sensitive probe for the cavity geometry. The interferograms can be modelled using the finite-difference time-domain method, and we demonstrate that a neural network trained on a library of these simulated patterns can be used to reconstruct the cavity depth. This approach establishes a proof of concept for AR-CL based depth reconstruction within a prescribed geometry and could form a route towards advanced three-dimensional metrology of complex nanostructures.
papers.tldr: A library of FDTD-simulated angle-resolved cathodoluminescence interferograms is used to train a neural network that reconstructs the depth of micrometer-scale cavities milled in gold, achieving a proof-of-concept depth RMSE of ~130 nm without sample tilting.

papers.title: Reconfigurable Chiral Phonons and Their Selection in Asymmetrically Stacked Graphene MoirMoir\'{e} Superlattices
authors: Yi-Fei Zhang, Ting-Ting Wang, Zhong-Jie Wang, Miao-Ling Lin, Yue Wang, Zi-Jian Zhong, Xue-Lu Liu, Heng Wu, Lin-Shang Chen, Yan-Meng Shi, Jin-Yang Lou, Lin-Han Li, Jia-Liang Xie, Rui Mei, Ti-Ying Zhu, Li-Fa Zhang, Jiang-Bin Wu, Ping-Heng Tan
papers.abstract: Chiral phonons, lattice vibrations carrying angular momentum, offer a new handle for controlling phonon-mediated phenomena in condensed matter, yet their on-demand generation and deterministic control remain challenging. Here we show, using helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy, that asymmetrically stacked graphene moir\'{e} superlattices provide a reconfigurable platform for chiral phonons. We observe a finite degree of circular polarization for both chiral interlayer shear phonons and intralayer optical phonons. A chiral-phonon Raman-tensor model attributes this response to interfacial $C_{2}$-symmetry breaking together with Raman resonance within the van Hove singularity region. Reversing either the twist sense or the stacking order inverts the degree of circular polarization through the spatial transformations linking the corresponding stacking geometries. By tuning the excitation energy and twist angle, we achieve nearly full-range control of the degree of circular polarization of interlayer shear phonons, from $-1$ to $1$, while gate-induced interlayer potential redistribution enables substantial and reversible in situ modulation. These results establish asymmetrically stacked graphene moir\'{e} superlattices as a versatile platform for generating and controlling chiral phonons, with implications for optoelectronic and quantum technologies.
papers.tldr: TLDR: Asymmetrically stacked graphene moiré superlattices provide a reconfigurable platform for generating and deterministically controlling chiral phonons, with helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy showing tunable circular polarization via twist sense, stacking order, excitation energy, and gate-induced interlayer potential.
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Angular Momentum Hall Effect of Axial Ferrons in Ferroelectrics
authors: Xiyin Ye, Tao Yu
papers.abstract: Phonon thermal and angular-momentum (AM) Hall effects are known in non-ferroelectric insulators, yet whether terahertz soft modes of displacive ferroelectrics, i.e., ``ferrons", share them remains open. We report axial ferrons that hold polarization-momentum locking in uniaxial ferroelectrics and show that both effects exist: a longitudinal temperature gradient drives a transverse AM flow without any field, whereas an out-of-plane magnetic field switches on the thermal Hall response. Two competitive channels emerge for the AM Hall effect: self-radiated magnetic fields hybridize two branches into circular modes whose momentum-locked Berry curvature deflects opposite magnetic moments to opposite edges, while temperature-gradient-induced mode quantum coherence adds a magnetic-moment dipole that leads to an opposite transverse AM current. An out-of-plane magnetic field breaks the exact polarization-momentum locking and yields a polarization Hall current. Numerical calculations show these effects are significant in both LiNbO$_3$ and van der Waals ferroelectrics. Edge magnetization or polarization accumulation can switch adjacent magnets or ferroelectrics, enabling low-power magnetoelectric functionality by thermal current in the future.
papers.tldr: The paper predicts that axial ferrons—terahertz soft modes in uniaxial ferroelectrics—exhibit thermal and angular-momentum Hall effects through polarization-momentum locking, with competing Berry-curvature and coherence-induced contributions and magnetic-field-switchable polarization Hall currents, enabling low-power magnetoelectric functionality in materials such as LiNbO₃ and van der Waals ferroelectrics.
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Antiferromagnetic phase of MnTe2: spin-order-induced renormalization of phonon Raman spectrum
authors: Taras Palasyuk, Ashutosh S. Wadge, Eduard E. Zubov, Igor Antoniazzi, Gayatri, Andrzej Wi\'sniewski, Wojciech Szuszkiewicz, Daniel Jastrzebski, Ryszard Diduszko, Adam Babi\'nski, Maciej R. Molas, Micha{\l} Wierzbicki, Cezariusz Jastrzebski
papers.abstract: Recently, two modes of spin wave excitations (magnons) were detected in Raman scattering spectra of MnTe2. It is an unconventional magnet that features a pyrite-type crystal structure hosting a non-collinear, non-coplanar antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin order below the N\'eel temperature. In this brief communication, the focus is primarily on the effect of spin ordering on lattice dynamics (phonons) that has been established through temperature (5 - 300 K), linear polarization angle (0 deg - 360 deg) and external magnetic field (up to 16 T) dependent measurements. It has been found that below the magnetic transition temperature, the frequencies of four out of five Raman-active lattice vibrations (i.e., Eg and three Tg phonon modes) revealed significant departure from the mechanism of the three-phonon anharmonic decay described by Klemens model. Here, we propose a new model considering spin-phonon coupling to explain frequency renormalization of the phonon part of the Raman spectrum upon the para-/antiferro- (PM/AFM) magnetic phase transition change in MnTe2. Through employing Green's function formalism, we show that a simple two-sublattice collinear antiferromagnet approach follows well both spin ordering induced hardening and softening of phonon modes observed in AFM phase of MnTe2 upon cooling. Additionally, the detailed temperature and field dependences of the energy for both magnon modes are presented. In addition to unexpected twofold anisotropy of the higher energy magnon mode (approx. 3.5 meV) unveiled in crossed configuration, our magneto-optical measurements revealed a subtle, yet definite softening trend for the lower energy mode (approx. 2.6 meV). Although the precise reasons for these effects remain unclear, we put forward a symmetry reduction in the local atomic surroundings as a possible mechanism for discussion.
papers.tldr: Spin ordering in the pyrite-type antiferromagnet MnTe₂ significantly renormalizes its Raman-active phonons below the Néel temperature, and a spin–phonon coupling model based on a two-sublattice collinear antiferromagnet explains both the hardening and softening of these phonon modes.

papers.title: Interface and film engineering for improved spin-charge interconversion in sputtered GeTe nanodevices
authors: S. Teresi, T. Frottier, M. Culot, W. Savero-Torres, P. Sgarro, M. Wissmann, A. Kandazoglou, F. Osana, J. Lagrave, D. T\'er\'eb\'enec, J. Paterson, A. Oysel Mestre, O. J. Mouawad, E. Chevilley, N. Bernier, P. No\'e, M. Bibes, F. Hippert, J. -P. Attan\'e, L. Vila, M. Cosset-Ch\'eneau
papers.abstract: Spin-logic devices promise non-volatile logic-in-memory computing with ultra-low power consumption, offering a route to circumvent the von Neumann bottleneck. Magnetoelectric and ferroelectric spin-orbit (MESO/FESO) devices, however, require spin-charge interconversion materials that combine a large output signal with properties that survive nanoscale integration. Tellurides are particularly fragile in this respect, as processing readily introduces defects that degrade their spin-charge interconversion properties. Here we demonstrate room-temperature spin-charge interconversion in patterned FESO nanoscale devices based on sputtered GeTe, with feature sizes down to 100 nm. By introducing a Ti interfacial layer between the CoFe electrode and GeTe, and by using GeTe films of improved crystalline quality, we increase the interconversion output signal from 3 m{\Omega} to 24 m{\Omega}, exceeding values reported for platinum at comparable device size. These results establish large-scale-deposited GeTe as a viable material platform for spin-logic devices and identify interface quality and film crystallinity as key levers for optimizing their performance.
papers.tldr: By inserting a Ti interfacial layer and improving GeTe film crystallinity, the authors boost room-temperature spin-charge interconversion in 100-nm-scale sputtered GeTe FESO nanodevices from 3 mΩ to 24 mΩ, establishing interface and film engineering as key routes to scalable GeTe spin-logic devices.

papers.title: Tunable first-order transitions and magnetic hysteresis in Bernal pentalayer graphene
authors: Wentian Zheng, Jiawei Hu, Yuxuan Yao, Fang Xie, Zihan Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Qimiao Si, Yonglong Xie
papers.abstract: In two-dimensional electron systems, strong Coulomb interactions can spontaneously lift flavor degeneracies such as spin and valley, producing first-order transitions with hysteretic switching of interest for memory devices. The subband degree of freedom in multiband systems may be viewed as a flavor that not only participates in such transitions but also enables control of the hysteretic behavior, as a displacement field can shift the energy difference between subbands. Here, we demonstrate this principle in Bernal-stacked pentalayer graphene, whose low-energy spectrum comprises a monolayer-like Dirac sub-band together with light and heavy bilayer-like sub-bands. Local compressibility measurements resolve a fully symmetry-broken Landau-level spectrum and a sequence of phase transitions that occur when Landau levels of different subbands cross, at which strong interactions redistribute the occupation among flavors. We show that these transitions exhibit hysteretic Hall responses in magnetic field, confirming their first-order character, and that the magnitude and sign of the hysteresis are tuned by the displacement field, as expected from the subband Landau-level ordering determined in compressibility measurements. Our work establishes the subband degree of freedom in multiband systems as a resource for engineering hysteretic switching, and highlights how local thermodynamic measurements can link microscopic insights to macroscopic responses in quantum materials.
papers.tldr: By using local compressibility measurements, the authors show that subband degrees of freedom in Bernal pentalayer graphene produce interaction-driven first-order phase transitions with magnetic hysteresis whose sign and magnitude can be tuned by a displacement field, establishing subbands as a resource for engineering hysteretic switching.

papers.title: Witnessing Gaussian Coexistence and Correlation-Ellipse Tomography
authors: Wanting Hou, Wei Liu, Hong-Chao Liu, Jun Xiong, Zhiyuan Ye
papers.abstract: Gaussian light is specified by second-order field moments, yet their hidden correlation geometry can demand higher-order intensity measurements. We establish a measurement hierarchy for "Gaussian coexistence", i.e., the simultaneous presence of cross covariance and cross pseudocovariance. For two zero-mean Gaussian modes with circular marginals, all unperturbed intensity moments of second or third order are blind to coexistence. In contrast, a balanced fourth-order residual provides a necessary and sufficient witness. Their identities, however, remain fundamentally ambiguous: recovering the two correlation strengths does not reveal which belongs to the covariance and which to the pseudocovariance. Unexpectedly, adding thermal fluctuations resolves this ambiguity: an independent, correlated thermal probe selectively modifies the covariance while leaving the pseudocovariance unchanged, allowing the two correlation strengths to be individually identified. Moreover, a coherent reference in only one arm then makes their relative phase accessible through third-order intensity correlation. Together, these measurements reconstruct a correlation ellipse and its Poincar\'e-sphere coordinates, determining the relative channel strengths and the ellipse orientation. The framework separates what intensity detection can witness, what thermal probing can identify, and what a single phase reference can orient, turning inaccessible Gaussian correlation structure into a quantitatively reconstructible geometry.
papers.tldr: The paper establishes a measurement hierarchy for Gaussian coexistence, showing that a balanced fourth-order intensity residual witnesses cross covariance and pseudocovariance, while thermal probing and a single phase reference resolve their ambiguity and enable reconstruction of the correlation ellipse and its Poincaré-sphere coordinates.

papers.title: Intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect in ferroaxial metals with high-order rotation axes
authors: Eleni Chatzikyriakou, Stepan Tsirkin, Fernando Pe\~naranda, Oscar Pozo, Ivo Souza, Fernando de Juan
papers.abstract: The low-field Hall resistivity of non-magnetic metals has an intrinsic quantum contribution that derives from the field-corrected Berry curvature and intrinsic magnetic moment of the Bloch states near the Fermi surface. However, its effect is usually overshadowed by the classical Lorentz-force contribution. Here we show that for the longitudinal Hall effect, which occurs in ferroaxial crystals when the applied magnetic field lies in the Hall plane, the Lorentz force contribution vanishes for the eight ferroaxial groups with a 3,4 or 6-fold rotation axis. This provides an opportunity to measure the quantum correction in isolation, but so far all measured instances of the effect fall in the remaining five ferroaxial groups of lower symmetry, where the Lorentz force dominates the signal. We compile a list of candidate ferroaxial metals with such high-order rotation axis and compute the Hall effect from first principles for representative candidates, identifying Ni$_3$P with $\sigma^{\rm H}_{xzx} = 28.4$ S/m/T as a promising material to unambiguously measure the intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect.
papers.tldr: This paper shows that in ferroaxial metals with 3-, 4-, or 6-fold rotation axes the Lorentz-force contribution to the longitudinal Hall effect vanishes—enabling isolated measurement of the intrinsic quantum Hall response—and identifies Ni\(_3\)P (\(\sigma^{\rm H}_{xzx}=28.4\) S/m/T) as a promising candidate material.
affiliations: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
Centro de Física de Materiales CSIC-UPV/EHU

papers.title: Magic-layer scenario for predicting non-van der Waals two-dimensional materials: The case of double-layer honeycomb structures
authors: Shota Ono
papers.abstract: A magic number is a specific size of a van der Waals (vdW) cluster that shows pronounced stability compared to adjacent sizes, and therefore magic clusters are preferentially formed in experiments. We apply the ``magic-layer'' concept to identify non-vdW two-dimensional (2D) materials that are difficult to exfoliate from their parent 3D crystals. As a case, we study the stability of thin films in III-V, II-VI, I-VII, and Mn-based compounds using first-principles calculations. By calculating excess energies for various thicknesses, we find significant stabilization reflecting the formation of double-layer honeycomb structures at specific thicknesses. The stability measure based on the magic-layer concept can distinguish the experimentally synthesized systems from the experimentally unrealized systems, which serves as a key descriptor for predicting the realization of non-vdW 2D materials.
papers.tldr: The paper introduces a “magic-layer” concept and a relative stability metric (\(M_2\)), based on first-principles thin-film energies, to predict stable non-van der Waals two-dimensional double-layer honeycomb materials by identifying thicknesses with anomalous stabilization and distinguishing experimentally realized from unrealized systems.

papers.title: Strain-enabled dynamical magnetoelectric coupling in BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$
authors: ChanJu You, Jayanti Higgins, Zhiren He, Yilin Evan Li, Harikrishnan KP, S\"oren Buchenau, Christo Guguschev, Mario Br\"utzam, Jiaqiang Yan, David Mandrus, David A. Muller, Darrell G. Schlom, Guru Khalsa, Ankit S. Disa
papers.abstract: Optical excitation has emerged as a powerful tool for manipulating and creating non-equilibrium phases of matter. Yet, the pathways available for optical control are intrinsically limited by the symmetries and interactions of the equilibrium system. Here, we demonstrate that these pathways can be redesigned through atomic-structural engineering to access hidden dynamical properties. By combining resonant vibrational excitation with epitaxial strain, we realize a light-induced, room-temperature multiferroic state in strained thin films of the technologically relevant hexagonal ferrimagnet, barium hexaferrite (BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$, BaM). Time-resolved second harmonic generation and magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements reveal an enhanced ferroelectric polarization together with a weakening of the magnetic moment upon exciting mid-infrared phonons in strained BaM thin films, but not in the bulk material. Structural analysis and first-principles-based theory show that this effect is enabled by strain-generated displacement of Fe$^{3+}$ ions, which break the local symmetry and facilitate an emergent dynamical magnetoelectric coupling. Both the strong lattice excitation and strain-induced symmetry breaking are essential for enabling this dynamical coupling, promising an important template for designing otherwise inaccessible non-equilibrium phenomena.
papers.tldr: Strain engineering combined with mid-infrared phonon excitation enables a room-temperature, light-induced dynamical magnetoelectric coupling in BaFe₁₂O₁₉ thin films by breaking local symmetry through Fe³⁺ displacements.

papers.title: Density-dependent photocarrier recombination in $\gamma$-InSe
authors: Vivek Jain, Salman Ahsanullah, Neema Rafizadeh, Gbenga S. Agunbiade, Hui Zhao
papers.abstract: We studied the photocarrier dynamics in $\gamma$-InSe using femtosecond transient reflectance spectroscopy. By measuring the dependence of the differential reflectance on the injected carrier density, we established an empirical relation between the optical response and carrier density, allowing quantitative analysis of the recombination dynamics. The carrier decay exhibits a strong density dependence, indicating a substantial contribution from nonlinear recombination. At high carrier densities, the dynamics are dominated by a second-order recombination process, with a rate constant of $3.8\times10^{-6}~\mathrm{cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At low densities, the decay becomes approximately exponential, with a carrier lifetime of about 7 ps. We also resolved an initial rise of the band-edge response with a time constant of less than 1 ps, which is attributed to hot-carrier cooling. These results reveal the competition between first-order and second-order recombination in $\gamma$-InSe and provide quantitative insights into its ultrafast photocarrier dynamics.
papers.tldr: Femtosecond transient reflectance measurements of hBN-protected 87-nm γ-InSe reveal density-dependent photocarrier recombination dominated by second-order recombination at high injection densities (rate constant \(3.8\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{cm^3\,s^{-1}}\)) and approaching an approximately 7-ps first-order lifetime at low densities, along with sub-1-ps hot-carrier cooling.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Topological High-Harmonic Spectroscopy for Characterizing Crystal Symmetries and Nonlinear Responses
authors: David Hervalejo-Sancho, Sergio Mart\'in-Domene, Rodrigo Mart\'in-Hern\'andez, Antonio Pic\'on, Luis Plaja, Jos\'e M. Caridad, Javier Serrano, Carlos Hern\'andez-Garc\'ia
papers.abstract: Structured light has emerged as a unique tool for probing nonlinear light-matter interactions. Particularly interesting is its interaction with anisotropic media, such as crystalline materials, whose anisotropic responses encode information about their electronic properties. Recently, topological high-harmonic spectroscopy was introduced as an all-optical approach to extract the anisotropic nonlinear response of graphene from harmonic spatial intensity profiles. Here, topological high-harmonic spectroscopy is combined with artificial intelligence (AI) to retrieve the anisotropic non-linear response and crystal symmetry of atomically thin materials. A convolutional neural network is trained and validated to learn the inverse mapping between harmonic far-field intensity profiles and the nonlinear response of materials exhibiting different rotational symmetries. Comparisons with microscopic high-harmonic-generation simulations demonstrate the accurate retrieval of distinct effective nonlinear responses in single-symmetry crystals, such as single-layer graphene and bilayer graphene with different stacking orders, and in crystals exhibiting multiple symmetry components, such as monolayer hexagonal boron nitride. Macroscopic high-harmonic-generation simulations assess the robustness and applicability limits of the technique. These results establish AI-assisted topological high-harmonic spectroscopy as a fast, contactless tool for characterizing nonlinear optical responses and crystal symmetries without phase-resolved measurements, opening prospects for applications to complex systems such as polycrystals and van der Waals heterostructures.
papers.tldr: This paper introduces AI-assisted topological high-harmonic spectroscopy, in which a convolutional neural network learns from harmonic far-field intensity profiles to retrieve the anisotropic nonlinear optical response and crystal symmetry of atomically thin materials without phase-resolved measurements.
affiliations: Instituto de Ciencia de Materiales de Madrid (ICMM-CSIC)

papers.title: Spin-Group versus Magnetic-Group Selection Rules for Nonlinear Photocurrents in Compensated Ferrimagnets
authors: Fu Li, Vikrant Chaudhary, Weiyi Pan, Hongbin Zhang, Harish K. Singh
papers.abstract: Optical excitation offers a contact-free, ultrafast route to charge and spin currents, with symmetry determining which nonlinear photocurrents are allowed and whether they carry charge, spin, or both. Spin-group symmetry describes the limit without spin-orbit coupling (SOC), whereas magnetic-group symmetry accounts for SOC. We show that the two descriptions yield different selection rules for both charge and spin photocurrents in the multiferroic compensated ferrimagnet GaFeO$_3$. Without SOC, only linear shift and circular injection currents are allowed, with identical components for charge and spin, so every charge current is spin polarized along the moments. SOC leaves these charge currents nearly unchanged, activates magnetic linear injection and circular shift charge currents, and enables pure spin currents polarized perpendicular to the moments. Ferroelectric switching reverses the linear shift and circular injection charge currents and their spin polarization. These findings establish the importance of magnetic-group symmetry for a complete description of nonlinear charge and spin photocurrents in compensated ferrimagnets.
papers.tldr: Spin-group and magnetic-group symmetries impose different selection rules for nonlinear charge and spin photocurrents in the compensated ferrimagnet GaFeO₃, with spin-orbit coupling activating additional magnetic injection/shift currents and pure spin currents whose charge-current counterparts are reversed by ferroelectric switching.

papers.title: Topological Narrow Bands in Twisted Rhombohedral Multilayer Graphene
authors: Alejandro Jimeno-Pozo, Danna Liu, Francisco Guinea, Pierre A. Pantale\'on
papers.abstract: Moir\'e graphene multilayers provide an atomically thin platform for engineering narrow topological bands through stacking, twist, and electrostatic control. Recent experiments on twisted rhombohedral graphene have revealed a high-Chern-number hierarchy determined by the number of rhombohedral layers. A microscopic description of this hierarchy requires connecting the ideal chiral picture to the realistic electronic structure. Here, we show that the two central moir\'e bands of twisted monolayer-$N$-layer rhombohedral graphene originate from hybridization between a monolayer Dirac cone and a rhombohedral surface state located at opposite corners of the moir\'e Brillouin zone. Increasing $N$ progressively narrows these bands, whereas reversing the displacement field transfers their wave-function weight between the twisted interface and the remote surface. In spectrally isolated regimes, this redistribution switches the lower band between Chern numbers $\mathcal{C}=N$ and $\mathcal{C}=-1$. A projected surface theory shows how interfacial tunneling is dressed by virtual propagation through the rhombohedral stack, explaining the field-selected Chern hierarchy and the recurring threefold structure of the real-space charge textures. These results establish layer number and displacement field as complementary nanoscale controls of band flatness, spatial polarization, and topology in graphene moir\'e heterostructures.
papers.tldr: The paper shows that in twisted monolayer–\(N\)-layer rhombohedral graphene, the two central moiré bands arise from hybridization between a monolayer Dirac cone and a rhombohedral surface state at opposite moiré Brillouin-zone corners, with layer number and displacement field controlling band narrowing, spatial polarization, and a field-switchable Chern-number hierarchy.

papers.title: Comparative Molecular Dynamics Study of Initial Oxide Film Growth on Al, Mg, and Ti Using a Universal Neural Network Potential
authors: Yoyo Hinuma, Taisuke Hasegawa
papers.abstract: Spontaneous formation of an oxide film, which may be passive, is found in many metals such as Al and Ti. We report direct computational observation of oxide film formation on the three major light structural metals, Al, Mg, and Ti, with molecular dynamics (MD) using a universal neural network potential (NNP). O2 molecules were supplied during MD simulations to replenish O consumed by the metal. Al and Ti formed a 1-2 nm thick film within a few ps of the simulation with O2 gas pressure of 102-103 atm. The film thicknesses of all metal oxides continued to increase proportionally to the logarithm of simulation time, consistent with Cabrera-Mott theory. Al and Ti oxides grow at the surface, while Mg oxide grows into the Mg metal. Al, Mg, and Ti are approximately 4.4, 4.3, and 5.2-fold coordinated, respectively, in the oxide.
papers.tldr: Using a universal neural network potential, molecular dynamics simulations show that Al, Mg, and Ti spontaneously form nanoscale oxide films with logarithmic Cabrera–Mott growth, where Al and Ti oxides grow at the surface while Mg oxide grows inward, with oxide coordinations of approximately 4.4, 4.3, and 5.2, respectively.

papers.title: Moir\'e-enabled polariton control in large-angle twisted bilayer graphene
authors: Bogdan Borodin, Xuanpu Zhang, Christopher Yang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Cyprian Lewandowski, Petr Stepanov
papers.abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP$^{3}$) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to $5.5^\circ$ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP$^{3}$ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above $4^\circ$ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moir\'e bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching $90\%$. Our results demonstrate that remote moir\'e bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.
papers.tldr: By probing large-angle twisted bilayer graphene with hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons, the authors show that hybridization between central and remote moiré bands creates a twist-angle-selected density window with strongly gate-tunable polariton wavelengths (up to ~90%), enabling reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons far from the magic angle.

papers.title: Non-integer high harmonic generation from many-body nonadiabatic gating
authors: Mingyao Guo, Luting Wang, Murali Suganya, Biqiong Yu, Martin Greven, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Raman Sankar, Yao Wang, David Hsieh
papers.abstract: High harmonic generation (HHG) in solids typically produces a rigid frequency comb locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. In strongly correlated materials, however, the light field can dynamically transform the electronic state on the timescale of harmonic generation itself, potentially violating this rule. Here, we report giant blueshifted, non-integer HHG in a cuprate Mott insulator Sr$_2$CuO$_3$ produced by mid-infrared excitations. Concurrent transient reflectivity measurements and time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model support a many-body temporal gating mechanism that suppresses light emission on the trailing edge of the pulse, thereby blueshifting radiated harmonics in the frequency domain. Our findings establish HHG emission energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many-body dynamics and pave the way for exploration and manipulation of correlated electronic phases of matter with strong-field spectroscopy.
papers.tldr: Researchers observed giant blueshifted, non-integer high-harmonic generation in the Mott insulator Sr₂CuO₃, explained by a many-body nonadiabatic temporal gating mechanism that suppresses trailing-edge emission and establishes HHG as a sensitive probe of correlated quantum dynamics.

papers.title: BEACON: Learning Observation-Conditioned Starting Points for Guided Conditional Flow Matching in Microscopy
authors: Anirban Ray, Florian Jug
papers.abstract: Fluorescence microscopy drives much of modern life science, but accessible imaging setups often yield images degraded by out-of-focus light, limited resolution, and strong signal-dependent noise. Computational restoration can recover high-quality images from such data, enabling cheaper and faster imaging at lower light dose, provided biologically meaningful structures are preserved. Guided conditional flow matching has recently shown strong results for microscopy dehazing and computational super-resolution by learning distributions of plausible restorations. However, it pairs each clean target with an independent standard Gaussian sample, so the starting point of every training path does not leverage the degraded observation. This arbitrary noise--target coupling can produce conflicting velocity targets and makes the conditional velocity field harder to learn. We present BEACON, a $BE$st-of-$K$ $A$daptive learned coupling for guided $CON$ditional flow matching, which learns an observation-conditioned base distribution. During training, a lightweight conditional noise model proposes $K$ starting points for each degraded input, and the candidate with the lowest flow-matching loss supervises both networks, while a KL term keeps the proposal close to the Gaussian prior. At inference, a single draw from the learned proposal is transported along the velocity field, requiring neither candidate selection nor the target. We evaluate BEACON on ten datasets spanning microscopy dehazing and computational super-resolution against 13 baseline families. BEACON achieves the best median perception--distortion rank for every pairing of a fidelity metric (PSNR, MicroMS-SSIM) with a perceptual metric (LPIPS, FID). Code and pretrained models will be released under a permissive license.
papers.tldr: BEACON improves guided conditional flow matching for microscopy restoration by learning an observation-conditioned starting distribution via a best-of-K adaptive coupling, yielding better perception–distortion trade-offs in dehazing and super-resolution.

papers.title: Emergent Electric-Field-Tunable $p$-Wave Magnetism in Twisted Bilayer NiPS$_3$
authors: Jiaran Su, Jin-Xin Hu, Qi Sun, Dante M. Kennes, Yuhao Fu, Lede Xian, Lijun Zhang
papers.abstract: A perpendicular electric field can reorient a momentum-space spin texture without changing the local magnetic configuration. In this Letter, we investigate this mechanism in a $21^\circ$-twisted $\mathrm{NiPS}_3$ bilayer with zigzag order and coplanar, nonparallel layer N\'eel vectors. In the ideal nonrelativistic limit, an antiunitary in-plane half-translation enforces opposite-spin pairing at opposite momenta, while a layer-exchanging twofold operation pins the leading $p$-wave spin splitting to a crystallographic direction. A perpendicular layer bias lifts this orientational constraint while preserving the antiunitary symmetry, allowing a transverse component of the splitting vector. First-principles calculations show gate-dependent reorientation and deformation of spin-resolved isoenergy contours. Wannier-based linear-response calculations further reveal field-activated diagonal spin conductivities and a polarity-dependent tilt in the angular profile of the transverse spin-current response. The spin-texture axis, dispersion axes, and transport-response axis are distinct quantities governed by the same symmetry reduction. These results identify layer bias as a route to controlling odd-parity spin textures and spin-current anisotropy, provided that the coplanar magnetic state remains stable.
papers.tldr: A perpendicular electric field in 21°-twisted bilayer NiPS₃ can controllably reorient and deform its odd-parity \(p\)-wave spin texture and activate anisotropic spin-current responses without altering the local magnetic order, enabling gate-tunable spin-texture and spin-transport control.
affiliations: Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter

papers.title: Curvilinear nanomagnets of non-trivial geometric topology
authors: Vagson L. Carvalho-Santos, Luke A. Turnbull, Na\"{e}mi Leo, Oleksandr V. Pylypovskyi
papers.abstract: In this Chapter, we focus on the question of how the global geometric characteristics given by the topology of the sample's shape are reflected in the properties of the magnetization field of the given curvilinear nanoarchitecture. We start with a brief introduction to differential geometry and topology, giving their connection to the specific properties of the vector field represented by the magnetization field defined at the specific manifold. Then we discuss modern fabrication and characterization techniques that make analysis of a sample's topology not only an interesting theoretical concept but also a directly accessible and practically relevant topic. The main attention of the Chapter is dedicated to the theoretical and experimental analysis of nanostructrures with the topology different from the extended films beyond the in-depth studied topic of tubes of the constant radius. In particular, toroidal, spherical, and non-orientable manifolds are considered.
papers.tldr: This chapter reviews how the global geometric topology of curvilinear magnetic nanostructures—such as toroidal, spherical, and non-orientable manifolds—governs the formation and properties of magnetization textures, linking differential geometry and topology with fabrication, characterization, theory, and experiments.

papers.title: From Weighted Frontier d-States to Geometric Descriptors for Atomically Dispersed Catalysts at the Molecule-Solid Crossover
authors: Yuqi Li, Zewen Wu, Longling Pang, Zhidan Li, Xianghua Kong
papers.abstract: Atomically dispersed catalysts exhibit molecule-solid crossover character when localized metal orbitals hybridize with support-derived bands, a regime not fully captured by either a d-band-center description or a frontier-orbital picture. We establish an electronic-to-geometric framework for oxygen reduction across fourteen metals. N-to-P substitution in M-N4 sites raises theoretical onset potentials in 13 systems, with Rh-N3P reaching 0.88 V, comparable to the Pt(111) benchmark. Scaling relations reduce *OOH, *O, and *OH thermodynamics to $\Delta$G*OH. M-N4 follows a dyz-dominated frontier-orbital picture, whereas M-N3P requires a weighted frontier d-state representation built from adsorption-relevant orbitals and their occupancies. The resulting $\epsilon$WFDS correlates with $\Delta$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.92, compared with 0.83 for the d-band center and 0.64 for the frontier-orbital. The identified roles of orbital occupancy and local coordination suggest an interpretable geometric descriptor, $\zeta$M-N3P = nd/rM-P, that predicts $\Delta$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.96. The ORR volcano analysis identifies strong-binding systems and motivates axial oxygen coordination. This design raises onset potentials by 0.70-2.46 V, and the M-N3PO descriptor predicts $\Delta$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.91. By bridging frontier-orbital and d-band-center descriptions, the framework provides a physically grounded electronic representation and a geometry-based screening route compatible with machine-learned interatomic potentials.
papers.tldr: The paper bridges frontier-orbital and d-band-center pictures via a weighted frontier d-state descriptor and converts it into a simple geometric descriptor, ζ_M-N3P = n_d/r_M-P, to predict *OH binding and guide the design of N-to-P-substituted, axially oxygen-coordinated atomically dispersed catalysts with enhanced oxygen-reduction activity.

papers.title: Noncontact Chemical and Morphological Profiling in Liquid via Fiber-Based Micro-FTIR
authors: Ching-Ping Chang, Jaehyeon Kim, Guanhua Qiao, Jonathan Matsuura, Jimai Chen, Lalith Krishna Samanth Bonagiri, Yiran Zhao, Yingjie Zhang
papers.abstract: Liquid-phase mid-infrared (MIR) imaging is challenging due to the strong MIR light absorption of most liquid media. Existing liquid-phase MIR microscopy approaches overcame the background absorption using predominantly either ultrathin liquid cells or attenuated total reflection (ATR) setups. However, these designs introduce additional challenges, such as sample confinement, limited probe volume, probe perturbation, and/or lack of quantification capabilities. In this work, a fiber-based Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) microspectroscopy method was developed to overcome the technical barriers of liquid-phase MIR characterization. By integrating a tapered fiber microprobe, a transmission-based optical setup, and a scanning stage, we achieved noncontact chemical and morphological profiling in liquid. The micro-FTIR capabilities were benchmarked by measuring a micropatterned photoresist substrate in water, obtaining quantitative spatial chemical distribution and morphological profiles with ~35 {\mu}m lateral resolution and nanometer-scale vertical detection limit. This noncontact, quantitative, liquid-phase micro-FTIR technique is promising for non-perturbative characterization of heterogeneous structures in liquids.
papers.tldr: A fiber-based micro-FTIR method enables noncontact, quantitative chemical and morphological profiling of liquid-phase samples with ~35 μm lateral resolution and nanometer-scale vertical sensitivity, avoiding thin-cell or ATR limitations.

papers.title: First-principles phase diagram of monolayer CrS$_2$ polymorphs under biaxial strain and its sensitivity to the Hubbard U parameter
authors: Rashmi Ranjan Routaray, Ali Ghojavand, Eric Bousquet
papers.abstract: In correlated two-dimensional magnets the balance between competing electronic and magnetic phases is often set by the strength of the on-site Coulomb interaction, so that the predicted ground state can hinge on a parameter that is not uniquely defined. Monolayer CrS$_2$ lies squarely in this regime, hosting several energetically close polymorphs whose character ranges from non-magnetic semiconducting to magnetically ordered metallic. We therefore investigate, using DFT$+U$ within the generalized gradient approximation, the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the 1H, 1T, 1T$'$, and 1T$''$ polymorphs of monolayer CrS$_2$ under varying Hubbard interactions ($U=0$--$8$~eV) and biaxial strain ($-10\%$ to $+10\%$). The 1T-derived structures remain metallic and magnetic throughout, with $U$ acting mainly as a spectral renormalization. The 1H phase behaves differently, passing from a non-magnetic semiconductor through an antiferromagnetic semiconducting regime before metallizing, so that the gap closes as $U$ increases while the local Cr moment grows monotonically. Biaxial tensile strain at fixed $U$ induces a similar sequence of transitions. Along both tuning pathways, the two inequivalent nearest-neighbor Cr--Cr exchange channels progressively separate and cross, with the parallel-spin channel becoming dominant, accompanied by a breathing-type bond disproportionation. Independent calculations with a localized-orbital implementation reproduce the overall evolution but yield shifted critical values of $U$ and of strain, demonstrating the robustness of the phase diagram while highlighting the implementation dependence of the transition thresholds.
papers.tldr: Using DFT+U, the authors show that monolayer CrS₂ polymorphs respond divergently to Hubbard U and biaxial strain—1T-derived phases remain metallic and magnetic, while 1H evolves from a nonmagnetic semiconductor to an antiferromagnetic semiconductor and then a metal via coupled electronic, magnetic, and lattice reorganization—with robust qualitative trends but implementation-dependent transition thresholds.
